items.name: Firefox ESR
items.tagline: The independent, open-source web browser by Mozilla.
description: Firefox ESR is the Extended Support Release of Mozilla’s browser — the same rendering engine and privacy protections as rapid Firefox, with a slower update cadence suited to desktops.
It ships with Enhanced Tracking Protection, sync via Firefox Account, and a large extension library.

items.name: Thunderbird
items.tagline: Email, calendar and chat — free and open source.
description: Thunderbird is Mozilla’s mail client: IMAP and POP support, OpenPGP end-to-end encryption, calendars and address books in one application.
The ESR build in Debian receives security updates on a stable schedule.

items.name: VLC
items.tagline: Plays everything — video, music, streams and discs.
description: VLC media player plays nearly every codec without external packs: files, network streams, DVDs and webcams, on every desktop platform.
It also converts formats, records screens and streams over the network. The Debian package is a metapackage that pulls in the player and its plugin set.

items.name: GIMP
items.tagline: The GNU Image Manipulation Program — raster editing, free.
description: GIMP is the free raster image editor: layers, masks, filters, content-aware tools and a scriptable plug-in system for photos, illustration and design work.
The 3.x series brings a modernised GTK interface and non-destructive editing improvements.

items.name: Blender
items.tagline: The complete open-source 3D creation suite.
description: Blender covers the full 3D pipeline — modelling, sculpting, animation, simulation, rendering, compositing and video editing — in one free application.
Cycles and EEVEE render engines ship built in, and the same file format runs on every platform.

items.name: Inkscape
items.tagline: Professional vector graphics editor, open standard SVG.
description: Inkscape is a vector editor built around the SVG standard: nodes, paths, booleans, text-on-path, extensions and a node editor for logos, icons and technical drawing.
It reads and writes AI-compatible SVG output, PDF, EPS and PNG.

items.name: LibreOffice
items.tagline: The free office suite — Writer, Calc, Impress and more.
description: LibreOffice is the open-source office suite: Writer (documents), Calc (spreadsheets), Impress (presentations), Draw, Base and Math, with strong Microsoft format compatibility.
The Debian package is a metapackage that installs the full suite.

items.name: Kdenlive
items.tagline: KDE’s non-linear video editor with unlimited tracks.
description: Kdenlive is a multi-track video editor built on MLT: proxy editing, effects, titling, audio mixing and timeline keyframes for real production work.
Projects render through FFmpeg to every common format.

items.name: Audacity
items.tagline: Multi-track audio recording and editing.
description: Audacity records live audio, digitises tapes and edits podcasts or music on a straightforward spectrogram-and-waveform view.
Noise reduction, EQ, compression and label tracks are built in; projects export to WAV, MP3, FLAC and more.

items.name: OBS Studio
items.tagline: Free streaming and screen recording, done properly.
description: OBS Studio records and broadcasts your desktop with scenes, sources, filters and hardware-accelerated encoding — a small studio in one window.
Streams to Twitch, YouTube and any RTMP endpoint, or records 4K locally.

items.name: Telegram Desktop
items.tagline: Fast, cloud-synced messaging client.
description: Telegram Desktop is the official client for Telegram: cloud chats, channels, voice calls and file sharing up to 2 GB, synced across every device.
On Debian the recommended route is the Flathub build, kept current by upstream.

items.name: Steam
items.tagline: Valve’s game platform — thousands of titles for Linux.
description: Steam is the game distribution platform: Proton runs Windows titles on Linux, and the library covers native Linux games, VR and remote play.
The Debian launcher package (in contrib) pulls in the Steam runtime on first start.

items.name: Claude Code
items.tagline: Anthropic’s agentic coding tool in your terminal.
description: Claude Code is a command-line agent for software engineering: it reads your project, edits files, runs commands and commits — under your direction, from the terminal.
Installed globally through npm; run claude inside a project to start.

items.name: Docker Engine
items.tagline: Build, ship and run containers everywhere.
description: Docker Engine packages applications into portable containers. The get.docker.com script installs the engine, CLI, containerd and compose plugin from Docker’s official apt repository.
After installing, the docker group manages access without sudo.

items.name: Node.js
items.tagline: JavaScript runtime built on Chrome’s V8 engine.
description: Node.js runs JavaScript outside the browser — servers, build tools and CLIs. The NodeSource setup script registers the official apt repository for the current LTS line.
npm ships with it, giving access to two million packages.

items.name: Git
items.tagline: The distributed version control system.
description: Git tracks projects of any size with fast branching and merging. It is the foundation of modern development workflows and every code host.
Debian’s build includes the CLI tools, gitk and the credential helpers.

items.name: Neovim
items.tagline: Vim’s refactor — hyperextensible, Lua-configured editing.
description: Neovim is a fork of Vim focused on extensibility: Lua configuration, built-in LSP support, tree-sitter syntax and a thriving plugin ecosystem.
It stays faithful to modal editing while modernising the internals.

items.name: SuperTuxKart
items.tagline: 3D kart racing with the open-source mascots.
description: SuperTuxKart is a family-friendly kart racer: circuits, arenas, football and story mode with split-screen and LAN/online multiplayer.
The engine package is small; the track data ships in companion packages.

items.name: 0 A.D.
items.tagline: Historical real-time strategy in the ancient Mediterranean.
description: 0 A.D. is a war and economy RTS covering the centuries around 500 BC – 500 AD: twelve civilisations, formations, real line-of-sight and naval warfare.
The engine package pairs with large data packages containing art, sound and maps.

items.name: Battle for Wesnoth
items.tagline: Turn-based fantasy strategy on an epic scale.
description: Battle for Wesnoth is turn-based strategy in a high-fantasy world: humans, elves, dwarves and orcs across dozens of single-player campaigns and hot-seat or online multiplayer.
Terrain and time of day shape every fight; the add-on server carries hundreds of community campaigns.
